articles.title: 'Something switched inside me': Nick Foles on his Super Bowl flow state and move behind the mic
articles.description: As he continues a foray into broadcasting with Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game, the Philadelphia folk hero reflects on fatherhood, flow states and outdueling Tom Brady Ask Nick Foles what he remembers most vividly about winning Super Bowl LII and he doesn’t mention the Philly Special , the brazen gadget play that passed straight into football folklore. Not the record 1,151 yards of combined offense or the nerve-shredding go-ahead touchdown drive or the surreal theater of a second-string quarterback outdueling Tom Brady on the biggest stage in American sports. Not even when Brady’s last-gasp Hail Mary pass fell harmlessly to the turf and the Philadelphia Eagles became champions of the National Football League for the first time since the Eisenhower administration. Instead, he remembers holding his daughter. Continue reading...

articles.author: Aaron Timms
articles.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
articles.description: For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Continue reading...

articles.author: Luke Entwistle
articles.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
articles.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says. Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 . “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.” Continue reading...

articles.author: Ed Aarons
articles.title: Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund
articles.description: Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the youngest player to appear in the Premier League , with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his highly anticipated debut . But after a week when Arsenal published an article dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager. Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match. articles.title: Lights go out on Commanders before they beat Bengals in final seconds
articles.description: Cincinnati Bengals 20-22 Washington Commanders Drew Stevens kicks game-winning field goal Game delayed after lights go out in third quarter Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired, and the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night. After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight-yard line. articles.title: Mets reportedly agree $450m contract with Tarik Skubal, richest deal for pitcher in MLB history
articles.description: Ace’s contract reportedly for nine years Mets have missed playoffs for last two seasons The New York Mets look to have sealed the biggest deal of MLB’s offseason by signing free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal. The New York Post’s Jon Heyman reported that the deal is worth $450m over nine years, the largest contract for a pitcher in baseball history. The previous record was for the $325m, 12-year deal Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers in 2024. Continue reading...

articles.description: Bears also continue strong start to season Ravens go down to sixth-straight loss The San Francisco 49ers (9-1) left Mexico City in control of the No 1 seed in the NFC after a convincing win over the Minnesota Vikings (7-3). Brock Purdy continued his brilliant season with three passing touchdowns, and the game was all but decided at half-time, when the Niners led 28-10. San Francisco’s win was marred after right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field after he suffered a serious leg injury. Continue reading...
